q.t: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 6 cm long and 4 cm wide (in cm).
q.e: Walk all the way round: two lengths and two breadths = 2 × (6 + 4).

q.t: Find the perimeter of a square of side 5 cm (in cm).
q.e: Four equal sides.

q.t: Find the area of a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm (in cm²).
q.e: 4 rows of 6 unit squares: length × breadth.

q.t: Find the area of a square of side 5 cm (in cm²).
q.e: 5 rows of 5 unit squares.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm (in cm).
q.e: Add all the sides.

q.t: Which unit is used for area?
q.e: Area counts unit squares, so it is measured in square units.

q.t: The perimeter of a shape is:
o: The total length of its boundary
q.e: ‘Peri’ means around and ‘meter’ means measure.

q.t: Find the perimeter of an equilateral triangle of side 7 cm (in cm).
q.e: Three equal sides.

q.t: A shape drawn on squared paper covers 9 full squares of 1 cm². Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Area is the number of unit squares covered.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a regular hexagon of side 3 cm (in cm).
q.e: Six equal sides.

q.t: A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and length 9 cm. Find its breadth (in cm).
q.e: Length + breadth = half the perimeter = 15.

q.t: A square has perimeter 36 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
A rectangle has area 72 cm² and length 9 cm. Find its breadth (in cm).
q.e: Breadth = area ÷ length.

q.t: A field is 20 m by 15 m. Find the cost of fencing it at ₹10 per metre (in ₹).
q.e: A fence goes round the edge: perimeter = 70 m, and 70 × 10 = 700.

q.t: A square has area 64 cm². Find its side (in cm).
Find the area of a rectangle 12 m by 7 m (in m²).
q.e: length × breadth.

q.t: How many square tiles of side 1 m are needed to cover a floor 5 m by 4 m?
q.e: Each tile covers 1 m², and the floor is 20 m².

q.t: Find the circumference of a circle of diameter 7 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm.
q.e: Circumference = π × diameter = 22/7 × 7.

q.t: A regular pentagon has perimeter 45 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: Five equal sides share 45 cm.

q.t: A rectangle is twice as long as it is wide and has perimeter 36 cm. Find its length (in cm).
q.e: Breadth b, length 2b: 2 × 3b = 36, so b = 6 and the length is 12.

q.t: A 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle is cut from one corner of a 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle. Find the area of the L-shape left (in cm²).
q.e: Whole − cut-out = 80 − 12.

q.t: A wire shaped as a square of side 12 cm is rebent into a rectangle 15 cm long. Find the area of the rectangle (in cm²).
q.e: The wire is 48 cm long, so length + breadth = 24 and the breadth is 9. Area = 15 × 9.

q.t: A square has the same area as a rectangle 25 m by 16 m. Find the side of the square (in m).
How many tiles 20 cm by 10 cm are needed to cover a wall 2 m by 1 m?
q.e: Wall = 200 cm × 100 cm = 20,000 cm². Each tile = 200 cm². 20,000 ÷ 200.

q.t: A wheel has diameter 70 cm. How far does it roll in one turn (take π = 22/7), in cm?
q.e: One turn covers its circumference: 22/7 × 70.

q.t: A rectangle has sides in the ratio 3 : 2 and perimeter 50 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Length + breadth = 25, shared 3 : 2 → 15 and 10. Area = 150.

q.t: The side of a square is made 4 times as long. Its area becomes how many times as large?
q.e: Both the length and the width are multiplied by 4: 4 × 4.

q.t: A room is 6 m by 4.5 m. Find the cost of carpeting it at ₹200 per m² (in ₹).
q.e: Carpet covers the floor: area = 27 m². 27 × 200.

q.t: A rectangle has the same perimeter as a square of side 10 cm, and its length is 13 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Perimeter = 40, so length + breadth = 20 and breadth = 7. Area = 13 × 7.

q.t: A park is 60 m by 40 m. Ravi jogs round its edge 5 times. How far does he jog (in m)?
q.e: One round = 200 m. Five rounds = 1000 m (1 km).

q.t: A lawn 12 m by 10 m has a path 1 m wide running all round it on the INSIDE. Find the area of the path (in m²).
q.e: The path takes 1 m off each end, leaving 10 m by 8 m of grass. 120 − 80 = 40.

q.t: A square and a rectangle both have perimeter 48 cm. The rectangle is 16 cm long. How much greater is the square’s area (in cm²)?
q.e: Square: side 12, area 144. Rectangle: 16 × 8 = 128. Difference 16.

q.t: A rectangle has area 180 cm² and perimeter 54 cm. Find its length (in cm).
q.k: max(l for l in range(1,27) if l*(27-l)==180)
q.e: Length + breadth = 27 and length × breadth = 180. The pair 15 and 12 fits both.

q.t: How many square tiles of side 25 cm are needed for a floor 5 m by 4 m?
q.e: 20 tiles fit along 5 m and 16 along 4 m: 20 × 16 = 320.

q.t: Three squares of side 4 cm are placed side by side in a row to make a rectangle. Find its perimeter (in cm).
q.e: The rectangle is 12 cm by 4 cm. The inner edges are hidden, so it is less than 3 × 16.

q.t: A circular garden has radius 14 m. A fence goes round it twice. Find the length of wire needed (take π = 22/7), in m.
q.e: One round = 2 × 22/7 × 14 = 88 m. Two rounds = 176 m.

q.t: When each side of a square is increased by 3 cm, its area increases by 39 cm². Find the original side (in cm).
The length of a rectangle is doubled and its breadth is halved. Its area:
q.e: 2 × length × ½ × breadth = length × breadth.

q.t: A 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle is cut from one corner of a 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle. Find the perimeter of the L-shape left (in cm).
q.e: The two new inner edges (4 and 3) exactly replace the pieces removed from the outside, so the perimeter is still 2 × (10 + 8).

q.t: A rectangle has whole-number sides and perimeter 20 cm. What is the greatest area it can have (in cm²)?
q.e: The sides add to 10: 1 × 9, 2 × 8, 3 × 7, 4 × 6, 5 × 5. The square, 5 × 5 = 25, is the largest.
